question: Have we trained the best R_theta we reasonably can before freezing it for every downstream experiment?
not_the_question: Does ordinary canonical-successor likelihood work? That is answered: 5.4603 -> 2.9238 from initialization, with within-family identity improving in all eight families.

run.intervention_policy: none unless actual divergence or persistent identity-capability regression

decision_rule_at_the_epoch_3_boundary.action: STOP and freeze, unless the curve is clearly still steep
CONSIDER epoch 4, but only on a fresh explicit decision -- no automatic continuation

improvement_is_measured_as: best eligible reference-law-weighted NLL at the epoch-3 boundary, minus 2.9238
why_a_threshold_of_0.05: The measured step-to-step resolution of this metric is ~0.026 nats -- steps 7,956 and 8,000, 44 optimizer steps apart, differ by that much on a deterministic evaluation. A 0.05 threshold is roughly twice the noise floor, so an improvement that clears it is resolvable rather than a wobble.

budget.note: Epoch 3 consumes most of the remaining margin. No epoch 4 without a new budget decision.

frozen_by_this_decision: the objective -- ordinary canonical-successor likelihood, unchanged
the corpus, sampling law, split and reserve
goal-marginal training is PARKED, not deleted: it must now earn entry by improving control cost, SMC ESS, mode coverage or oracle efficiency, not by rescuing R_theta
